title: When the Protocol Sings Anew
premise: Wendell Nystrom has spent thirty years alone on Kepler Station, tending a seed vault and the beacon that hums to no one—until the ship Meridian returns from deep space carrying colonists who have aged backward into children with their memories intact. The reversal was caused by the beacon itself, which Wendell discovers was never commissioned by any human authority but is a listening protocol left by something older, still broadcasting coordinates. As the reactor powering the station begins an irreversible countdown, Wendell and the child-crew of the Meridian must cross dead space to reach the relay and silence or answer the signal before it draws whatever wrote it. They reach the relay in time to send one message—an inheritance of choice rather than obedience—and Wendell, staying behind as the station burns, finally becomes the gardener his garden was always meant for.
about_author: Ada Villalobos is a former botanist who traded greenhouses for word processors after a decade cataloguing seed banks across three continents. She writes quiet, aching science fiction about people who keep things running long after anyone remembers why.

chapters.title: The Garden for Nobody
chapters.summary: In Wendell's POV, we inhabit the ritual of his solitary life: pruning vault-trees, logging the beacon's pulse, talking to seeds meant for generations unborn. When the Meridian appears against all odds, he assumes hallucination. The emotional beat is loneliness cracking open into terror and hope as the airlock opens on children wearing adult faces.

chapters.title: Children of the Long Dark
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Captain Ilsa Reyes-Mbeki, now eleven years old, commanding a crew of reversed adults who remember careers they can no longer perform. They piece together that the beacon's signal caused their reversal—and that it predates humanity's arrival. The beat is grief braided with resolve: they must reach the relay before the reactor's countdown ends.

chapters.title: Dead Space Sonata
chapters.summary: Alternating POV as the Meridian crosses the silent dark toward the relay, pursued by the beacon's growing song. Wendell confronts the truth that he was hired to maintain a trap, not a lighthouse; Ilsa must trust the man who unknowingly aged her crew backward. Climax: the relay wakes, and something answers.

chapters.title: What We Leave Growing
chapters.summary: At the relay, Wendell chooses to stay and broadcast a final message—an inheritance of consent, not command—while Ilsa pilots the children home through the closing countdown. The station burns behind them; the signal goes quiet, then sings anew, gentler. The beat is bittersweet resolution: survival purchased at the price of one life, freely given.
